paras.text: E-commerce (E-Commerce)
paras.urdu: ای کامرس (E-Commerce):
paras.pashto: برېښنايي سوداګري (E-Commerce)

paras.text: By e-commerce is meant electronic commerce (Electronic Commerce). In brief it is also called e-commerce (E Commerce) or EC (EC). In Urdu this term is used for it: trade by means of electric (electronic) instruments, or electronic trade. Its meaning is: buying and selling goods and services (Goods & Services) by means of electronic instruments, delivering goods to the customer, and receiving or paying the amount. In the system of electronic instruments the internet (internet) and computer network (Computer Network) etc. are included.
paras.urdu: ای کامرس سے مراد ہے الیکٹرانک کامرس (Electronic Commerce)۔ اسے مختصراً ای کامرس (E Commerce) یا ای سی (EC) بھی کہتے ہیں۔ اردو میں اس کے لئے یہ اصطلاح استعمال ہوتی ہے: تجارت بذریعہ برقی آلات یا برقیاتی تجارت۔ اس کا مطلب ہے: اشیاء و خدمات (Goods & Services) کو برقی آلات کے ذریعہ خریدنا، بیچنا، گاہک تک مال پہنچانا اور رقم کی وصول یا ادائیگی کرنا۔ برقی آلات کے نظام میں انٹرنیٹ (internet) اور کمپیوٹر کے نیٹ ورک (Computer Network) وغیرہ شامل ہیں۔
paras.pashto: له برېښنايي سوداګرۍ مراد الیکټرانیک کامرس (Electronic Commerce) دی. په لنډه توګه ورته اي کامرس (E Commerce) یا اي سي (EC) هم وايي. په اردو کې ورته دا اصطلاح کارېږي: د برېښنايي وسایلو له لارې سوداګري، یا برېښنايي سوداګري. مطلب یې دا دی: د توکو او خدمتونو (Goods & Services) د برېښنايي وسایلو له لارې پېرل، پلورل، پېرودونکي ته مال رسول او د پیسو اخیستل یا ورکول. د برېښنايي وسایلو په نظام کې انټرنېټ (internet) او د کمپیوټر شبکه (Computer Network) او نور شامل دي.

paras.text: In other words, by e-commerce is meant bringing into operation modern information technology (Information Technology: IT) in trade and business, and taking benefit from it. In short, these matters are included in e-commerce: (i) transfer and transmission (Transfer) of money by means of electronic instruments; (ii) electronic marketing; (iii) online buying and selling; (iv) exchange of business information by means of electronic instruments; (v) the system of automatic machines (Automated); (vi) the automatic electronic system of providing information about trade.
paras.urdu: بالفاظِ دیگر ای کامرس سے مراد ہے تجارت اور کاروبار میں جدید اطلاعاتی ٹیکنالوجی (Information Technology: IT) کو بروئے کار لانا اور اس سے فائدہ اٹھانا۔ غرض ای کامرس میں یہ اُمور شامل ہیں: (i) رقم کی منتقلی اور ترسیل (Transfer) بذریعہ برقی آلات۔ (ii) برقیاتی مارکیٹنگ۔ (iii) آن لائن خرید و فروخت۔ (iv) کاروباری معلومات کا تبادلہ بذریعہ برقی آلات۔ (v) خودکار مشینوں (Automated) کا نظام۔ (vi) تجارت کے بارے میں اطلاعات کی فراہمی کا خودکار برقیاتی نظام۔
paras.pashto: په بل عبارت له برېښنايي سوداګرۍ مراد په سوداګرۍ او کاروبار کې د عصري معلوماتي ټکنالوژۍ (Information Technology: IT) کارول او له هغې ګټه اخیستل دي. لنډه دا چې په برېښنايي سوداګرۍ کې دا چارې شاملې دي: (i) د برېښنايي وسایلو له لارې د پیسو لېږد (Transfer)؛ (ii) برېښنايي بازارموندنه؛ (iii) انلاین پېر و پلور؛ (iv) د برېښنايي وسایلو له لارې د سوداګریزو معلوماتو تبادله؛ (v) د اتومات ماشینونو (Automated) نظام؛ (vi) د سوداګرۍ په اړه د معلوماتو د برابرولو اتومات برېښنايي نظام.

paras.text: In brief, in e-commerce the technology of electronic news-giving, i.e. IT (Information Technology), is used; e.g. internet (Internet), extranet (Extranet), e-mail (E-Mail), electronic books (E-books), mobile phone and other computer networks (Networks) etc.

paras.text: In the modern age, for e-commerce the more suitable term web commerce (Web Commerce) has been established, i.e. buying and selling goods and services by means of the net of the world level (World Wide Web: www), payment and collection by means of electronic instruments, and further the use of credit cards (Credit Card) etc. Up to 1994 the use of the web (Web) became very popular, and by 2000 most business institutions in America and Western Europe had established their web sites (Web Sites). sections.theory:
E-commerce (E-Commerce)

By e-commerce is meant electronic commerce (Electronic Commerce). In brief it is also called e-commerce (E Commerce) or EC (EC). In Urdu this term is used for it: trade by means of electric (electronic) instruments, or electronic trade. Its meaning is: buying and selling goods and services (Goods & Services) by means of electronic instruments, delivering goods to the customer, and receiving or paying the amount. In the system of electronic instruments the internet (internet) and computer network (Computer Network) etc. are included.

In other words, by e-commerce is meant bringing into operation modern information technology (Information Technology: IT) in trade and business, and taking benefit from it. In short, these matters are included in e-commerce: (i) transfer and transmission (Transfer) of money by means of electronic instruments; (ii) electronic marketing; (iii) online buying and selling; (iv) exchange of business information by means of electronic instruments; (v) the system of automatic machines (Automated); (vi) the automatic electronic system of providing information about trade.

In brief, in e-commerce the technology of electronic news-giving, i.e. IT (Information Technology), is used; e.g. internet (Internet), extranet (Extranet), e-mail (E-Mail), electronic books (E-books), mobile phone and other computer networks (Networks) etc.

In the modern age, for e-commerce the more suitable term web commerce (Web Commerce) has been established, i.e. buying and selling goods and services by means of the net of the world level (World Wide Web: www), payment and collection by means of electronic instruments, and further the use of credit cards (Credit Card) etc. Up to 1994 the use of the web (Web) became very popular, and by 2000 most business institutions in America and Western Europe had established their web sites (Web Sites). By 2005 e-commerce became very popular in North America, Western Europe and some countries of East Asia, e.g. South Korea etc., but in the backward and developing countries of the Third World (Third World) it has not yet become prevalent. However, gradually it is being introduced here too. By 2005 the value of the volume of electronic business (i.e. e-commerce) in the whole world was more than twelve arab (Billion) dollars.

Inflation (Inflation)

In the previous pages it has been stated that by the increase of the quantity of money the value of money (Value Money) becomes less, and by the quantity of money becoming less the value of money increases. Besides the quantity of money, some other causes also affect the value of money. The name inflation (Inflation) and deflation (Deflation) is given to these two different economic conditions. Thus in this chapter we discuss inflation, its causes, consequences and remedy.

Definition of inflation (Inflation) (Definition)

By inflation is meant:

“The increase in prices which arises in that situation when the use and expenditure of money is increasing, but there is not a proportionate increase (Proportionate Increase) in the production (Output) of goods.”

E-commerce (E-Commerce)

By e-commerce is meant electronic commerce (Electronic Commerce). In brief it is also called e-commerce (E Commerce) or EC (EC). In Urdu this term is used for it: trade by means of electric (electronic) instruments, or electronic trade. Its meaning is: buying and selling goods and services (Goods & Services) by means of electronic instruments, delivering goods to the customer, and receiving or paying the amount. In the system of electronic instruments the internet (internet) and computer network (Computer Network) etc. are included.

In other words, by e-commerce is meant bringing into operation modern information technology (Information Technology: IT) in trade and business, and taking benefit from it. In short, these matters are included in e-commerce: (i) transfer and transmission (Transfer) of money by means of electronic instruments; (ii) electronic marketing; (iii) online buying and selling; (iv) exchange of business information by means of electronic instruments; (v) the system of automatic machines (Automated); (vi) the automatic electronic system of providing information about trade.

In brief, in e-commerce the technology of electronic news-giving, i.e. IT (Information Technology), is used; e.g. internet (Internet), extranet (Extranet), e-mail (E-Mail), electronic books (E-books), mobile phone and other computer networks (Networks) etc.

In the modern age, for e-commerce the more suitable term web commerce (Web Commerce) has been established, i.e. buying and selling goods and services by means of the net of the world level (World Wide Web: www), payment and collection by means of electronic instruments, and further the use of credit cards (Credit Card) etc. Up to 1994 the use of the web (Web) became very popular, and by 2000 most business institutions in America and Western Europe had established their web sites (Web Sites). By 2005 e-commerce became very popular in North America, Western Europe and some countries of East Asia, e.g. South Korea etc., but in the backward and developing countries of the Third World (Third World) it has not yet become prevalent. However, gradually it is being introduced here too. By 2005 the value of the volume of electronic business (i.e. e-commerce) in the whole world was more than twelve arab (Billion) dollars.

Inflation (Inflation)

In the previous pages it has been stated that by the increase of the quantity of money the value of money (Value Money) becomes less, and by the quantity of money becoming less the value of money increases. Besides the quantity of money, some other causes also affect the value of money. The name inflation (Inflation) and deflation (Deflation) is given to these two different economic conditions. Thus in this chapter we discuss inflation, its causes, consequences and remedy.

Definition of inflation (Inflation) (Definition)

By inflation is meant:

“The increase in prices which arises in that situation when the use and expenditure of money is increasing, but there is not a proportionate increase (Proportionate Increase) in the production (Output) of goods.”

افراطِ زر (Inflation)

گزشتہ اوراق میں یہ بیان کیا گیا ہے کہ زر کی مقدار بڑھ جانے سے زر کی قدر (Value Money) کم ہو جاتی ہے، اور زر کی مقدار کم ہو جانے سے زر کی قدر بڑھ جاتی ہے۔ زر کی مقدار کے علاوہ بعض دیگر اسباب بھی زر کی قدر کو متاثر کرتے ہیں۔ ان دو مختلف معاشی حالتوں کو افراطِ زر (Inflation) اور تفریطِ زر (Deflation) کا نام دیا جاتا ہے۔ چنانچہ اس باب میں ہم افراطِ زر، اس کے اسباب، نتائج اور علاج پر بحث کرتے ہیں۔

افراطِ زر (Inflation) کی تعریف (Definition):

افراطِ زر سے مراد ہے:

”قیمتوں میں اضافہ، جو اس صورت میں پیدا ہوتا ہے جب روپیہ کا استعمال اور مصرف بڑھ رہا ہو، لیکن اشیاء کی پیداوار (Output) میں متناسب اضافہ (Proportionate Increase) نہ ہو۔“

“By the rate of inflation is meant that percentage rate during a particular period at which prices may be going on increasing.”

[S. Fischer’s English definition is summarised:] the inflation rate is the percentage rise in prices per period. (S. Fischer)

$\text{Inflation in 2012} = \dfrac{\text{CPI in 2012} - \text{CPI in 2011}}{\text{CPI in 2011}} \times 100$

In other words, by it is meant such an economic situation when the value of the rupee is falling and prices are rising. This arises at that time when the balance of demand and supply of goods is disturbed, i.e. demand is more but supply less. An economist has said in a very beautiful way that:

“When much money runs after few things, then understand that inflation has appeared.”

Consequences of inflation (Consequences of Inflation)

The following dreadful consequences of inflation emerge:

(i) Prices continuously rise; (ii) in the race of the quantity of money and the quantity of goods, production lags behind; (iii) prices and wages chase each other, i.e. they increase because of each other; (iv) hoarding (Hoarding), black marketing (Black Marketing), and the system of price control and rationing start to become prevalent; (vi) the rate of interest and profit on financial assets and investment becomes low, because of which savings are discouraged; (vii) among people the tendency of collecting non-monetary assets (Non-Monetary Assets), e.g. lands, buildings, property etc., increases and the trend of investment becomes slow; (viii) by the mutual relation of the prices of different goods becoming unclear, disorder occurs in the allocation (Allocation) of productive resources and inputs (Input), from which the process of economic growth (Growth) is affected; (ix) because of inflation competitive power in international markets decreases, the exchange rate (Exchange Rate) of domestic currency becomes unfavourable, and the balance of external payments (Balance of Payments) is disturbed; (x) the poor and the fixed-income class are badly affected, because the greater part of their income is spent on food items.

Rate of inflation (Rate of Inflation)

The rate of inflation is stated thus:

“By the rate of inflation is meant that percentage rate during a particular period at which prices may be going on increasing.”

[S. Fischer’s English definition is summarised:] the inflation rate is the percentage rise in prices per period. (S. Fischer)

The method of measuring the rate of inflation or the rate of increase in prices is this: finding out the percentage change in prices during a particular year; e.g. to measure the rate of inflation during 2010 and 2011 the following formula will be used:

$\text{Inflation in 2012} = \dfrac{\text{CPI in 2012} - \text{CPI in 2011}}{\text{CPI in 2011}} \times 100$

(Read from the left side.) In words: inflation in 2012 = (index of consumer prices in 2012 minus index of consumer prices in 2011) ÷ index of consumer prices in 2011 × 100 per cent.

[If in 2010 the CPI is] 150 and in 2011 it is 165, then the rate of inflation will be this: (read from left to right) … (continued on p.210)

sections.text:
بالفاظِ دیگر اس سے مراد ایسی معاشی صورتِ حال ہے جب روپیہ کی قدر کم ہو رہی ہو اور قیمتیں چڑھ رہی ہوں۔ یہ اس وقت پیدا ہوتی ہے۔ جب اشیاء کی طلب اور رسد کا توازن بگڑ جائے یعنی طلب زیادہ ہو، لیکن رسد کم۔ ایک ماہرِ معاشیات نے بڑے خوبصورت انداز میں کہا ہے کہ:

”جب تھوڑی چیزوں کے پیچھے زیادہ روپیہ بھاگے تو سمجھیے کہ افراطِ زر رونما ہو چکا ہے۔“

افراطِ زر کے نتائج (Consequences of Inflation):

افراطِ زر کے درج ذیل خوفناک نتائج برآمد ہوتے ہیں:

(i) قیمتیں مسلسل چڑھتی جاتی ہیں، (ii) مقدارِ زر اور مقدارِ اشیاء کی دوڑ میں پیداوار پیچھے رہ جاتی ہے، (iii) قیمتیں اور اُجرتیں ایک دوسرے کا تعاقب کرتی ہیں، یعنی ایک دوسرے کی وجہ سے بڑھتی جاتی ہیں۔ (iv) ذخیرہ اندوزی (Hoarding)، چور بازاری (Black Marketing)، پرائس کنٹرول راشننگ سسٹم کا رواج ہونے لگتا ہے۔ (vi) مالی اثاثوں اور سرمایہ کاری پر شرح سود و منافع کم ہو جاتی ہے، جس کے باعث بچتوں کی حوصلہ شکنی ہوتی ہے۔ (vii) لوگوں کے اندر غیر زری اثاثے (Non-Monetary Assets) مثلاً زمینیں، عمارتیں، جائیداد وغیرہ جمع کرنے کا میلان بڑھ جاتا ہے اور سرمایہ کاری کا رجحان ماند پڑ جاتا ہے۔ (viii) مختلف اشیا کی قیمتوں کی باہمی نسبت غیر واضح ہو جانے سے پیداواری وسائل اور مداخل (Input) کی تخصیص (Allocation) میں گڑبڑ ہو جاتی ہے جس سے معاشی نشو و نما (Growth) کا عمل متاثر ہوتا ہے۔ (ix) افراطِ زر کے باعث بین الاقوامی منڈیوں میں مقابلیاتی قوت گھٹ جاتی ہے، ملکی کرنسی کی شرحِ مبادلہ (Exchange Rate) غیر موافق ہو جاتی ہے۔ اور بیرونی ادائیگیوں کا توازن (Balance of Payments) بگڑ جاتا ہے۔ (x) غریب اور معینہ آمدنی والا طبقہ بُری طرح متاثر ہوتا ہے کیونکہ ان کی آمدنی کا بیشتر حصہ اشیائے خوراک پر صَرف ہو جاتا ہے۔

افراطِ زر کی شرح (Rate of Inflation):

افراطِ زر کی شرح یوں بیان کی جاتی ہے:

”افراطِ زر کی شرح سے مراد ہے ایک خاص عرصہ کے دوران وہ فی صد شرح جس پر قیمتیں بڑھتی جا رہی ہوں۔“

[ایس۔ فشر کی انگریزی تعریف کا خلاصہ:] افراطِ زر کی شرح فی عرصہ قیمتوں میں فیصد اضافہ ہے۔ (S. Fischer)

افراطِ زر کی شرح یا قیمتوں میں اضافہ کی شرح ناپنے کا طریقہ یہ ہے: ایک خاص سال کے دوران قیمتوں میں فی صد تبدیلی معلوم کرنا، مثلاً 2010ء اور 2011ء کے دوران افراطِ زر کی شرح ناپنے کے لئے ذیل فارمولا استعمال کیا جائے گا:

$\text{Inflation in 2012} = \dfrac{\text{CPI in 2012} - \text{CPI in 2011}}{\text{CPI in 2011}} \times 100$

(بائیں طرف سے پڑھیں) 2012ء میں افراطِ زر = 2012ء میں صارفین کی قیمتوں کا اشاریہ منفی 2011ء میں صارفین کی قیمتوں کا اشاریہ ÷ 2011ء میں صارفین کی قیمتوں کا اشاریہ × 100 فیصد

[اگر 2010ء میں صارفین کی قیمتوں کا اشاریہ] 150 ہو اور 2011ء میں 165 ہو، تو افراطِ زر کی شرح یہ ہو گی: (بائیں سے دائیں پڑھیں) … (ص 210 پر جاری)
